## The story so far

Five days of classes, ABCs, dataclasses, and properties all built toward one
goal: a clean, testable pipeline from raw fab databases to an actionable finding.
This capstone runs the full workflow — no new OOP concepts, just the toolkit
doing its job.

**The hypothesis:** a gate-etch timing drift on chamber C2 in LOT003 caused an
above-spec Vth shift on wafers W10–W18.

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

ELEC_DB = Path("../../data/electrical.db")
PROC_DB = Path("../../data/process.db")
```

---

## 1 · Extract

```{python}
from fab_toolkit import ElectricalSource, ProcessSource, Pipeline

elec = ElectricalSource(ELEC_DB)
proc = ProcessSource(PROC_DB)

# Sanity check: each source on its own
elec_all = elec.fetch()
proc_all = proc.fetch()
print(f"Electrical: {elec_all.shape}  columns: {list(elec_all.columns)}")
print(f"Process:    {proc_all.shape}  columns: {list(proc_all.columns)}")
```

---

## 2 · Join

`Pipeline` aggregates electrical to per-wafer mean TFT Vth and process to
per-wafer ETCH_GATE duration, then inner-joins on (lot_id, wafer_id).

```{python}
pipeline = Pipeline(elec, proc)
joined = pipeline.run()

print(f"Joined: {joined.shape}  — one row per (lot, wafer)")
joined.head()
```

```{python}
# Distribution of ETCH_GATE duration: LOT003 wafers should stand out
joined.groupby("lot_id")[["mean_tft_vth", "etch_gate_s"]].agg(["mean", "std"]).round(3)
```

The signal is clear already: LOT003's `etch_gate_s` mean is ~25 s above the
other lots, and its `mean_tft_vth` is ~0.05 V higher.

---

## 3 · Model — OLS regression

```{python}
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

model = smf.ols("mean_tft_vth ~ etch_gate_s", data=joined).fit()
print(model.summary().tables[1])   # coefficient table only
```

```{python}
# Coefficient and confidence interval in plain numbers
coef  = model.params["etch_gate_s"]
ci_lo, ci_hi = model.conf_int().loc["etch_gate_s"]
pval  = model.pvalues["etch_gate_s"]
r2    = model.rsquared

print(f"Coefficient:  {coef:.5f} V/s  (95% CI [{ci_lo:.5f}, {ci_hi:.5f}])")
print(f"p-value:      {pval:.2e}")
print(f"R²:           {r2:.3f}")
```

The positive, significant coefficient confirms the direction: longer etch →
higher Vth. The effect size (~0.002 V per second) is physically plausible for a
gate-etch process.

---

## 4 · Spec analysis with `VthAnalysis`

```{python}
from fab_toolkit import ElectricalDB, WaferDataset, SpecLimits, VthAnalysis

db  = ElectricalDB(ELEC_DB)
tft = WaferDataset.from_db(db, device_type="TFT")

spec = SpecLimits("vth", lower=0.40, upper=0.46)
print(f"Spec window: [{spec.lower}, {spec.upper}] V\n")

rows = []
for lot_id in tft.lots():
    lot_data = tft.data[tft.data["lot_id"] == lot_id]
    a = VthAnalysis(lot_data, spec)
    rows.append({"lot_id": lot_id, "yield_pct": round(a.yield_pct, 1), "n_fails": a.n_fails})

pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

---

## 5 · Wafer map

```{python}
from plotnine import (
    ggplot, aes, geom_tile, geom_point,
    scale_fill_gradient2, scale_color_gradient2,
    facet_wrap, coord_fixed, labs, theme_bw, theme, element_text
)

# Per-site mean Vth across all wafers, faceted by lot.
site_means = (
    tft.data
    .groupby(["lot_id", "x", "y"])["vth"]
    .mean()
    .reset_index(name="mean_vth")
)

vth_mid = tft.data["vth"].quantile(0.5)

wafer_map = (
    ggplot(site_means, aes("x", "y", fill="mean_vth"))
    + geom_tile(width=18, height=18)
    + scale_fill_gradient2(
        low="#2166ac", mid="white", high="#d6604d", midpoint=vth_mid,
        name="Mean\nVth (V)"
    )
    + facet_wrap("lot_id", nrow=1)
    + coord_fixed()
    + labs(title="Mean TFT Vth per PCM site — LOT003 is the outlier",
           x="x (mm)", y="y (mm)")
    + theme_bw()
    + theme(figure_size=(14, 3), strip_text=element_text(size=9))
)
wafer_map.draw()
```

---

## 6 · Regression scatter

```{python}
from plotnine import geom_smooth, scale_color_manual, guides, guide_legend

# Flag the defect lot for visual callout
joined["group"] = joined["lot_id"].apply(
    lambda l: "LOT003 (drift)" if l == "L003" else "L001/L002/L004/L005"
)

scatter = (
    ggplot(joined, aes("etch_gate_s", "mean_tft_vth", color="group"))
    + geom_point(size=2.5, alpha=0.8)
    + geom_smooth(aes(group="1"), method="lm", color="black", se=True, size=0.8)
    + scale_color_manual(values={"LOT003 (drift)": "#d6604d",
                                  "L001/L002/L004/L005": "#4393c3"})
    + labs(
        title=f"TFT Vth vs ETCH_GATE duration  (R²={r2:.2f}, p={pval:.1e})",
        x="ETCH_GATE step_seconds (s)", y="Mean TFT Vth (V)", color="Lot group"
    )
    + theme_bw()
    + theme(figure_size=(8, 5))
)
scatter.draw()
```

## 7 · Report

The rendering of this `.qmd` file *is* the report — Quarto produces the HTML.
The `ReportRenderer` classes from Day 4 are used here to emit a brief text
summary, illustrating the Open/Closed pattern one last time:

```{python}
from fab_toolkit import MarkdownRenderer, HTMLRenderer

l003_yield = next(r["yield_pct"] for r in rows if r["lot_id"] == "L003")
baseline_yield = sum(r["yield_pct"] for r in rows if r["lot_id"] != "L003") / 4

summary_sections = {
    "Finding": (
        f"LOT003 wafers W10–W18 show a Vth excursion of ~0.05 V above baseline.\n"
        f"LOT003 yield: {l003_yield:.1f}%  vs baseline average: {baseline_yield:.1f}%."
    ),
    "Root cause": (
        f"ETCH_GATE step_seconds drifted +~25 s on chamber C2 for the affected wafers.\n"
        f"OLS: Vth = {model.params['Intercept']:.4f} + {coef:.5f} × etch_gate_s "
        f"(R²={r2:.2f}, p={pval:.1e})."
    ),
    "Recommendation": (
        "Inspect chamber C2 ETCH_GATE recipe; review maintenance log for the\n"
        "period covering LOT003 processing."
    ),
}

# The same sections rendered two ways without touching existing classes:
print(MarkdownRenderer().render(summary_sections))
```

```{python}
# Save an HTML summary alongside the notebook
from pathlib import Path
HTMLRenderer().save(summary_sections, Path("lot003_summary.html"))
print("Saved lot003_summary.html")
```

---

## What the class hierarchy bought us

| Component | Pattern | Payoff |
|---|---|---|
| `ElectricalDB` | class with state + methods | SQL filter building in one place; swappable DB path |
| `WaferDataset` | @classmethod constructors + dunders | Consistent construction from any source; native container feel |
| `DataSource` ABC | abstract base class | Enforces the fetch() contract; makes Pipeline testable with stubs |
| `ElectricalSource` | composition + ABC | Wraps ElectricalDB without duplicating SQL; swappable in Pipeline |
| `Pipeline` | composition of two DataSources | Join logic isolated; depends on interface not implementation |
| `SpecLimits` / `KpiSpec` | frozen @dataclass | Immutable config; free eq/repr; hashable |
| `PrepConfig` | @dataclass + field(default_factory) | Mutable config builder; mutable-default trap avoided |
| `VthAnalysis` | @property + validated setters | Computed yield always consistent; invalid bounds caught immediately |
| `ReportRenderer` | ABC + Template Method | Add new formats without touching existing code |

The workflow that took five notebooks and scattered functions is now:

```python
joined = Pipeline(ElectricalSource(ELEC_DB), ProcessSource(PROC_DB)).run()
model  = smf.ols("mean_tft_vth ~ etch_gate_s", data=joined).fit()
```

Testable, swappable, readable.
